page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 8 virtual CPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 3.525 GHz. Compute resources are supplemented by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, providing solid single-core throughput alongside AVX, AES, and SHA hardware extensions.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local ephemeral storage is bundled with this configuration, requiring attached remote disks such as Premium SSDs for persistent data. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses out of the box.

Synthetic testing places the single-core CPU throughput in the top 25 percent of assessed hardware, supported by a 2702.98 stress-ng single-core score. Multi-core compute and overall application performance remain balanced across median tiers, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5893.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 11885.13. Measured memory read bandwidth is consistent across typical block sizes, though large-block write operations register at a lower 24.52 GB/sec, reflecting a potential bottleneck for heavy sequential memory writes.

The balanced hardware distribution makes this instance well matched for medium-scale web serving, internal business applications, enterprise microservices, and continuous integration runners. Applications requiring sustained sequential disk performance or unmetered local input/output must factor in the latency and provisioning costs of attached storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D8as_v5 is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 3.525 GHz, supported by 32.0 GB of RAM in a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options like Premium SSDs. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong single-core performance alongside dependable multi-core execution, reflected in solid results across Geekbench, PassMark, and Redis operations, though uncached memory write throughput presents a slight bottleneck. Given its configuration and balanced resource density, the instance fits typical enterprise workloads, mid-tier relational databases with remote storage, application microservices, and web servers.
